court: Court of Appeals for the First Circuit

issues.label: Jurisdiction over consolidated petitions
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction over both petitions and the effect of the BIA’s reconsideration order on the earlier petition.

issues.label: Final order and mootness
issues.why: The court must decide whether the June 4, 2025 BIA order supersedes the March 7, 2025 order and moots or alters review of the first petition.

issues.label: Timeliness of each petition
issues.why: The court must ensure each petition for review was filed within the statutory deadline for the relevant final order.

issues.label: Exhaustion of issues
issues.why: The court may review only claims and arguments properly exhausted before the BIA unless an exception applies.

issues.label: Standard of review allocation
issues.why: The court must apply de novo review to legal questions and substantial-evidence review to factual findings, including mixed questions under the correct framework.

issues.label: Scope of record on review
issues.why: Review is limited to the administrative record, so the court must exclude extra-record factual material and assess any record-completeness disputes.

issues.label: Adequacy of agency reasoning
issues.why: The court must determine whether the IJ/BIA provided reasoned consideration and addressed material evidence and arguments.

issues.label: Credibility finding consequences
issues.why: Because the IJ found Muchiri credible, the court must treat his testimony as accepted unless the agency made other valid limiting findings.

issues.label: Removability charge validity
issues.why: The court must confirm the INA §237(a)(1)(B) overstay charge and NTA/proceedings were legally sufficient, to the extent contested or jurisdictionally relevant.

issues.label: Asylum statutory eligibility
issues.why: The court must decide whether the accepted facts satisfy asylum eligibility requirements under 8 U.S.C. §1101(a)(42)(A).

issues.label: Past persecution legal sufficiency
issues.why: The court must assess whether the harms found amount to “persecution” as a matter of law given severity, frequency, and context.

issues.label: Protected-ground nexus
issues.why: The court must determine whether persecution was “on account of” a protected ground and whether the agency applied the correct nexus standard.

issues.label: Particular social group validity
issues.why: If “family” is the asserted PSG, the court must assess cognizability (immutability/particularity/social distinction) and correct application of circuit law.

issues.label: Family-based persecution analysis
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the harm was because of familial membership versus purely personal or criminal motives.

issues.label: Alternative protected grounds
issues.why: The court must determine whether religion/political opinion/other PSG theories tied to Mungiki involvement were raised, exhausted, and properly analyzed.

issues.label: Persecutor identity relevance
issues.why: The court must address whether harm by the father, age mates, and Mungiki members constitutes persecution by private actors requiring state inability/unwillingness (or by de facto authorities).

issues.label: Government inability/unwillingness (past)
issues.why: For past persecution by non-state actors, the court must assess whether the agency correctly evaluated Kenya’s ability or willingness to protect Muchiri at the time.

issues.label: Presumption from past persecution
issues.why: Having found past persecution, the court must confirm the correct rebuttable presumption of future persecution was applied.

issues.label: Rebuttal—fundamental change in circumstances
issues.why: The court must determine whether substantial evidence supports the agency’s finding of fundamental changed circumstances sufficient to rebut the presumption.

issues.label: Adult status as changed circumstance
issues.why: The court must assess whether becoming an adult is a legally and factually sufficient “fundamental change” for fear rebuttal in this context.

issues.label: Country-conditions change assessment
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether evidence supports that Kenya’s efforts against Mungiki materially reduce the specific risk to Muchiri.

issues.label: Individualized risk vs general conditions
issues.why: The court must decide whether the agency improperly relied on generalized improvements without addressing individualized likelihood of targeting.

issues.label: Burden-shifting correctness
issues.why: The court must ensure the government bore the burden to rebut the presumption once past persecution was found.

issues.label: Internal relocation feasibility
issues.why: The court must consider whether internal relocation was addressed where relevant, including who bears the burden and whether relocation would be reasonable.

issues.label: Future persecution independent of presumption
issues.why: If the presumption is rebutted, the court must evaluate whether Muchiri established an independent well-founded fear of future persecution.

issues.label: Well-founded fear components
issues.why: The court must apply the correct subjective and objective components and the correct probability threshold.

issues.label: Humanitarian asylum eligibility gateway
issues.why: The court must confirm that past persecution was established and that the fear presumption was rebutted (or otherwise) before reaching humanitarian asylum.

issues.label: Humanitarian asylum—compelling reasons
issues.why: The court must assess whether the agency applied the correct standard for “compelling reasons” based on severity and lasting effects of past persecution.

issues.label: Humanitarian asylum—other serious harm
issues.why: The court must assess whether the agency properly evaluated a reasonable possibility of “other serious harm” unrelated to a protected ground.

issues.label: Childhood persecution weighting
issues.why: The court must consider whether the agency properly accounted for the applicant’s age at the time of harm when evaluating severity and future risk.

issues.label: Matter of L-S- application
issues.why: The court must determine whether the BIA correctly applied Matter of L-S- factors to the record facts.

issues.label: Discretionary asylum denial validity
issues.why: Because the IJ stated asylum would be denied in discretion, the court must decide whether discretion was properly exercised and supported by lawful factors.

issues.label: Discretionary factors and due process
issues.why: The court must assess whether the IJ relied on arrests/encounters without convictions, improper evidence, or inadequate findings in exercising discretion.

issues.label: BIA review of discretionary ruling
issues.why: The court must determine whether the BIA adopted/affirmed a discretionary denial and whether that limits judicial review under jurisdiction-stripping provisions.

issues.label: Withholding—correct legal standard
issues.why: The court must ensure the “clear probability” (more likely than not) standard and correct nexus standard for withholding were applied.

issues.label: Withholding not automatic from asylum
issues.why: The court must address whether the IJ/BIA incorrectly treated asylum denial as necessarily dispositive of withholding despite different elements (e.g., discretion, bars, burdens).

issues.label: Withholding—future persecution analysis
issues.why: The court must decide whether the agency made an adequate, individualized assessment of future persecution risk for withholding.

issues.label: Withholding—state action requirement
issues.why: For private-actor harm, the court must assess whether the agency correctly required and analyzed government inability/unwillingness for future harm.

issues.label: CAT—torture definition application
issues.why: The court must determine whether the agency applied the regulatory definition of torture, including severity and specific intent.

issues.label: CAT—likelihood assessment
issues.why: The court must assess whether substantial evidence supports the finding that torture is not more likely than not.

issues.label: CAT—public official involvement
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the agency correctly analyzed torture “by or at the instigation of or with consent or acquiescence” of officials.

issues.label: CAT—acquiescence/willful blindness
issues.why: The court must ensure the correct legal standard for acquiescence (including willful blindness) was applied to Kenyan police conduct.

issues.label: CAT—individualized evidence
issues.why: The court must determine whether the agency properly considered individualized threats from Mungiki and any police corruption/complicity evidence.

issues.label: CAT—past harm relevance
issues.why: The court must assess whether the agency properly weighed past harm as predictive evidence for CAT even if harms occurred in childhood.

issues.label: BIA reconsideration scope correctness
issues.why: The court must review whether the BIA properly corrected factual errors and whether its revised reasoning cured prior defects.

issues.label: BIA factual error materiality
issues.why: The court must decide whether the BIA’s initial misstatement about harm sources indicates inadequate review or prejudicial error requiring remand.

issues.label: Adoption vs independent BIA reasoning
issues.why: The court must identify whether review targets the IJ decision, the BIA decision, or both, depending on the BIA’s mode of affirmance.

issues.label: Substantial evidence support overall
issues.why: The court must determine whether a reasonable adjudicator would be compelled to reach a contrary conclusion on key factual findings.

issues.label: Legal error vs factual dispute separation
issues.why: The court must distinguish legal misapplication (reviewable) from factual weighing (deferential) across asylum, withholding, and CAT rulings.

issues.label: Procedural due process in hearings
issues.why: The court must consider any claims that the IJ denied a full and fair hearing, limited testimony, or failed to develop the record.

issues.label: Notice and opportunity to respond
issues.why: If the IJ/BIA relied on country reports or discretionary factors, the court must ensure Muchiri had notice and a chance to rebut.

issues.label: Translation/interpretation issues
issues.why: Any interpretation problems could affect fairness and must be addressed if raised or apparent in the record.

issues.label: Counsel effectiveness concerns
issues.why: If prior counsel errors are alleged, the court must assess whether an ineffective-assistance claim was properly presented under Lozada and exhausted.

issues.label: Statutory bars to asylum/withholding
issues.why: The court must confirm whether any mandatory bars (e.g., particularly serious crime, serious nonpolitical crime, persecution of others, terrorism) apply or were improperly assumed.

issues.label: Mungiki characterization relevance
issues.why: The court must consider whether the agency’s shifting description (cult/tribe/gang/religion) affected protected-ground or risk analyses.

issues.label: Persecution vs criminal harm distinction
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether harms were treated as private criminality rather than persecution tied to a protected ground, and whether that was correct.

issues.label: Relief-specific burdens of proof
issues.why: The court must ensure correct burdens were applied separately for asylum, withholding, and CAT after presumption rebuttal.

issues.label: Remand necessity standard
issues.why: If errors exist, the court must decide whether they are harmless or require remand for agency factfinding under ordinary remand principles.

issues.label: Stay of removal implications
issues.why: The court must address any pending stay issues or whether removal affects jurisdiction and available remedies.
